products.name: Stado
products.category: Infrastructure / compute and queue control plane
products.one_line: Policy-controlled queue and compute control plane for machines you own or authorize.
products.selection_note: The widest command surface we ship: a Clap-style noun tree over jobs, hosts, quota and credits. Study how a large control-plane CLI keeps its top-level help to one screen of verbs and pushes detail into per-command help.
products.sub_note: Per-command help exists and is the documented way down one level.

products.name: Skarbiec
products.one_line: Credential and authentication management for the AI era.
products.selection_note: The only product here whose help is machine-readable JSON rather than prose, and the only one whose first refusal is a state gate rather than a parse error. Study what a credential CLI is willing to say before a vault exists.
products.sub_note: Skarbiec has no per-subcommand help; the subcommand is reached before argument parsing and answers with the vault state gate instead.

products.name: Weles
products.one_line: Authorized browser execution for AI agents, with signed receipts.
products.selection_note: A CLI whose real work is gated on an authorization boundary, so its safe surface is help and identity only. Study how a product that refuses unauthorized work advertises that boundary in its own usage text.
products.sub_note: Weles exposes no per-subcommand help. `weles version` is the only subcommand that can be run here without authorizing a workflow or touching durable onboarding state, so that is the subcommand surface this record measures.

products.name: Jeden
products.category: Agents / autonomous coding and company building
products.one_line: The autonomous agent for building software and running the loop around it.
products.selection_note: A single-block usage synopsis for an agent runtime whose flags are permission grants (`--allow-write`, `--allow-command`, `--yolo`). Study how a dangerous capability set is presented in first-run help.
products.sub_note: Jeden's help is one usage block covering every subcommand; there is no per-subcommand help. `jeden run --help` is not a safe probe: when probed once outside this recording it resolved credentials through Skarbiec before parsing `--help` and failed with an HTTP 403, so this record measures `jeden version` instead and reports that finding rather than re-running it.

products.name: Probierz
products.category: Quality / test execution and evidence boundary
products.one_line: The quality-evidence boundary: selection, execution, evidence, and verdicts.
products.selection_note: The one product whose refusal is a structured machine-readable failure envelope rather than a usage dump. Study a CLI that answers an unknown surface with a parseable `probierz-failure` line plus one plain sentence.
products.sub_note: Probierz has no per-subcommand help: `--help` after a subcommand is read as a surface name and refused. That refusal is the observed subcommand surface.

products.name: Oko (oko-cli)
products.one_line: Understand your team's interactions with AI.
products.selection_note: A headless companion CLI with one flat usage block and no version form at all. Study the cost of that: the same text answers help, an unknown flag, and a subcommand help request, and only the exit status distinguishes them.
products.sub_note: Oko answers a subcommand help request with the whole top-level usage block.

products.name: Singularity
products.one_line: An open-source framework for autonomous agents that execute tasks and manage resources.
products.selection_note: The narrowest installed surface in the catalog: one subcommand, `onboarding`. Study a product whose CLI deliberately exposes only the first-use journey.
products.sub_note: argparse gives every subcommand its own help; `onboarding` is the only one.

products.name: Tama (tama-cli)
products.category: Policy / agent and Git hook catalog
products.one_line: Your AI agent made a mistake? Tama creates rules so that it never happens again.
products.selection_note: A policy catalog CLI that answers `--help` after a subcommand by ignoring the flag and running the read-only command. Study how a hook installer separates a plan from an install.
products.sub_note: Tama ignores a trailing `--help` and executes the subcommand; `install-plan` only reports the paths an install would touch, so nothing is written.

products.name: Transcript Lake
products.one_line: Nothing you ever told an AI is lost again.
products.selection_note: The only help here that opens with a `Start safely:` section and names the read-only commands first. Study help text that is ordered by risk rather than alphabetically.
products.sub_note: Per-command usage exists and prints one line of purpose with its flags.

products.name: Transcript Label Trainer
products.category: Models / local classifiers over transcript labels
products.one_line: Small models for your custom harness needs.
products.selection_note: An argparse CLI that states its own boundary in the help body — 'Never writes to the lake.' Study a product that publishes what it will not touch above its command list.
products.sub_note: argparse gives every subcommand its own help.
